#
# Pinned to an exact binary rather than a version range because bpy is a stateful

variant.note: A full-height projection: a shallow three-storey pavilion 4 m wide and 0.6 m out, two windows a floor, finished with a deep cornice and a flat tin deck where a house's main roof would take it over.

windows.why_not_ordinary: a basement light under each of the bay's windows, read off the 1888 plate: about 0.95 m across and 1.0 m high, its head at the plate's 1.2 m, flat-headed under a rock-faced course and filled with a scrolled iron grille (T-2916). T-3129: the grille as the c. 1888 Chicagology photograph shows it (chicagology_photo, x 278-362 px, y 1175-1276 px): a flat-bar frame round the light with a border about 0.12 m wide of short bars about 0.06 m apart (uprights across the head and foot, rungs up the sides), and inside it a square panel with a small rosette at its centre, eight spokes out to a ring about 0.44 m across, a volute curling in each corner and a smaller one on the middle of each side. The pattern is read off the photograph; its sizes are scaled from it against the light's 0.95 m, and the leaves on the scrolls are below what the bar can carry. The photograph also takes the light lower than the plate's reading: through its camera the head lands on the plate's line (y 1176 px against the render's 1178) but the foot sits 14 px lower (y 1277 against 1263) over a plinth half as deep. T-3133 lowers it towards the photograph's foot: its head kept at 1.22 m and its sill brought down from 0.22 to 0.17 m, the light 1.05 m, by halving the bay's plinth to 0.05 m (the bay's `plinth_m`) and keeping the 0.02 m of wall the kit leaves between the plinth and the K06 sill laid under the light, so the plinth and sill together make the photograph's pale ledge under the grille, which reads about 0.15 m (y 1276-1290 px at the bay's 89.2 px a metre). The photograph's foot (y 1276 px) stands about 0.10 m over the bay's foot (1285): the build's stands 0.07 m higher, the sill's 0.10 m less the plinth's 0.05 m given up, which no lower plinth recovers while the kit lays a sill under every light

the canted north face's one light a storey, read off the 1888 plate at x 92-107 px (about 0.6-0.87 of the face from the wall, about 0.65 m across seen obliquely) at the front windows' sill and head; built at the K06 ordinary least width, 0.75 m (T-2988)

the canted north face's one light a storey, read off the 1888 plate at x 92-107 px (about 0.6-0.87 of the face from the wall, about 0.65 m across seen obliquely) at the front windows' sill and head; built at the K06 ordinary least width, 0.75 m (T-2988)

variant.note: A canted upper oriel at the first floor, 1.3 m of front and 0.65 m out, carried on four stone courses stepped back into the wall, under a steep copper hip.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the oriel's three tall narrow transomed lights, read off the 1888 plate at about 0.5 m each between stone mullions over a 2.8 m front
the oriel's south return's narrow transomed lights, read off the 1888 plate at x 473-491 px, close-set on a return 0.73 m long (three there; two of 0.2 m are what the return holds)

The plan is the kit's rectangle sheared onto the sheet's parallelogram (skew_per_m 0.303: each metre south along the west wall steps it 0.303 m east; widths and openings are laid out along the lot line, so on the slanting walls each is about 4% longer than its s range). Turned to the lot: there is no alley here, so the kit's alley wall, with the carriage bay, is the WEST wall, facing the house's yard, and the kit's yard wall is the back wall to the tracks. The kit's party wall, which has no opening, stands at the north end, 0.7 m inside the 1709/1721 lot line; the open gable faces south over the rest of 1721's yard and is built without openings, because the sheet marks its wall with the fire-wall sign. On the west wall the carriage bay (3.0 m clear) under a loft hatch at its north end, then a stable sash, a man door and a second stable sash along the 14.8 m wall, each under a loft sash; on the back wall two sash, each under a loft sash. The kit's 40-degree gable roof with its ridge along the slant. No stair, ramp, lean-to, wing, workyard or ventilator: the sheet draws none, and no drive to the building is drawn or built.

capitals.read: east-wing gable pair (W 7.2-14.7). HABS 13 (level, about 21.4 px/ft): a block capital about 28 px (1.3 ft) across, its lower half rounded in to the shaft, dark curls at its upper corners under a carved band, a raised mass at its middle; HABS 14 the same block. The band's and body's motifs are too small in either print to read and are reconstructed

tower-shoulder pair (W 25.8-32.9). A utility pole crosses it in both prints; HABS 13 shows the block's edges either side of the pole at the east pair's width and the same rounded-in foot. Its carving is reconstructed, cut unlike the east pair's and the seven front capitals, as the museum's 2013 post says every one of the nine differs
sheet 6: a slotted band over crossing straps
sheet 6: a zigzag band over a ring of radiating leaves
sheet 6 and the museum's 2013 close-up 'capital 2' (a18-ghm-blog-capital-2-2013): a band of diamonds, a square block under it, corner volutes and a basket-weave body

over the front door: the museum's 2013 close-up (a18-ghm-blog-capital-hhr-2013) and blog text, Richardson's monogram (two mirrored R's on an H, boxed) in a large ring under a checkerboard band; sheet 6 draws the band and the box
sheet 6 and the museum's 2013 close-up 'capital 1' (a18-ghm-blog-capital-1-2013): a band of discs, two stems crossing in a V up to corner volutes, a lozenge between
sheet 6: a band of discs over a round boss between scrolls
sheet 6: a band of discs over a cross-hatched (basket-weave) body

coach_house.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick and the sheet's window mark is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1700-stable-1932. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, walls '12 8' (north) and '12' (south), a stable's X over the whole, and one of the key's window marks, on the alley wall about 9.74 m from the north wall line and 9.63 m from the south, with a dot for each storey (openings in both storeys there). It draws no fire-wall sign on this building. The kit stands as drawn: its party wall at the north end, where the building's north wall stands on the lot line; its open gable at the south end, 2.9 m short of the 1706/1712 lot line and 10.6 m short of 1712's stable, with no opening, as the sheet marks none. Every opening's s counts from the party wall's inner face (the alley wall's from the north end, the yard wall's from the south end, as the kit lays them). The mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, centred where it stands (s 9.41). The carriage bay (3.0 m clear) with the loft hatch over it toward the north end, a man door with a loft sash over it, and a second stable sash with a loft sash over it toward the south end are the kit's, spaced along the longest alley wall in the package; the yard wall has a door onto the workyard at its middle between four stable sash, with loft sash over the outer two. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at 30 degrees over the 10.42 m span, about 3.0 m from eave to ridge, as the deep stables (1616, 1612, 1626, 1628, 1736) took over 11-15 m. No external stair, ramp, lean-to, wing or ventilator: the sheet draws none. Not built: the sheet's dashed L inside the building, 1.29 m in from the east wall and 1.66 m in from the south (the census's dashed partition), which divides the inside and shows nothing outside; and its solid dot about 2.8 m from the south wall and 7.3 m from the alley, the key's sign for a vertical steam boiler (the kit has no stack, and the sheet draws none). The workyard is paved from the yard door to the pair's shared rear wall line, 22.6 m east of the yard wall, between the two townhouses' rear ranges; the walk takes the middle because which household the stable served is not read.

variant.note: A canted upper oriel at the first floor, 1.3 m of front and 0.65 m out, carried on four stone courses stepped back into the wall, under a steep copper hip.

windows.why_not_ordinary: an oriel's cheek light: narrower than an ordinary sash so it fits the canted cheek

coach_house.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick and the sheet's two window marks is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1612-stable-1932. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, walls '12 8', a stable's X over the whole, a dashed frame partition 7.87 m from the alley, and two of the key's window marks: on the alley wall about 8.38 m from the north wall line with a dot for each storey (openings in both storeys there), and on the north wall about 9.29 m from the alley line with one dot (an opening in one storey, built in the first as 1620's one-dot mark is). It draws no fire-wall sign on this building. The kit is built in MIRROR IMAGE (`mirror`): its party wall stands at the south end, against 1616's party wall 0.38 m away (the sheet draws the two wall lines apart, rows 2117 and 2124.5), and its open gable at the north end, which faces 1608's open rear yard and carries the sheet's one-dot mark. Every opening's s counts from the party wall's inner face (the alley and yard walls' s from the south end and the north end respectively, as the kit lays them; the gable's from the alley face). The alley wall carries a stable sash and a loft sash over it where its mark stands, a man door with a loft sash over it toward the south end, and the kit's carriage bay (3.0 m clear) toward the north end with the loft hatch over it; the yard wall a door onto the workyard at its middle between two stable sash and two loft sash; the north gable one stable sash where the sheet's mark stands and nothing over it. The south end's party wall rises the kit's 0.45 m above the roof, where the sheet draws no fire-wall sign: the kit has no second open gable, and the south end is the one that stands hidden against 1616's taller party wall. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at 30 degrees (1736's, 1812's and 1616's deep-stable pitch) over the 14.02 m span, about 4.0 m from eave to ridge; whether the yard part, first seen in 1911, ran under one roof with the alley part or under its own is not read, and one roof is built. No external stair, ramp, lean-to, wing or ventilator: the sheet draws none. Not built: the frame partition (inside), the sheet's solid dot near the south-east corner (the key's vertical steam boiler; the kit has no stack and the sheet draws none) and a small cross near the south end of the alley wall that the key does not explain. The workyard is paved from the yard door to the house's rear wing, 13.0 m east of the yard wall.

current_inputs_doc.blender_pin:
# Pinned Blender for the content build. tools/bake.sh verifies the hash before use.
#
# Pinned to an exact binary rather than a version range because bpy is a stateful
# tool whose defaults and operators shift between releases; version pinning is what
# buys back determinism. The bpy pip wheel is a documented fallback, but the binary
# is preferred: the wheel hard-couples Blender's minor version to a specific CPython,
# which makes agent sandboxes fragile.
#
# Verified working 2026-08-09: headless geometry, custom float attributes, smart UV
# project, Cycles CPU AO bake, GLB export — all green in ~0.8 s for a test mesh.

BLENDER_VERSION=4.5.3
BLENDER_URL=https://download.blender.org/release/Blender4.5/blender-4.5.3-linux-x64.tar.xz
BLENDER_SHA256=975c58fcb244273838534bba771e64ad87739216b0f9b39a888531a49a72d845
BLENDER_DIR=blender-4.5.3-linux-x64

# Fallback, if the binary cannot run in a given environment:
#   pip install bpy==4.5.*        # requires Python 3.11

The sheet gives the outline of a stable 9.76 m along the alley by 7.83 m deep, of a one-storey range 8.33 m on south of it along the alley and as deep, to 1736's coach house, and of a one-storey piece 3.87 m deep by 3.12 m against the stable's yard wall at its north end; '2' storeys and '1' and '1'; the brick; walls '12 12' on the lot line and '12 8' between the stable and the range; the key's fire-wall sign with two ticks at the alley end of the stable's north wall and of its south wall; and two of the key's window marks: one on the stable's alley wall 5.47 m from its north wall line and 4.29 m from its south, a dot for each storey (openings in both storeys there), and one on the range's alley wall 4.44 m from the stable's south wall line, with one dot. No stable's X (the 1886 plate crosses it) and no use lettered. The kit stands as drawn: its party wall at the north end, on the lot line, where the sheet draws one wall against 1726's building and 1726's record already stands its own party wall (two 13-inch walls back to back, each inside its own building's outline, against the sheet's one line, in the liberty); its open gable at the south end, which the range covers to 3.45 m and which is otherwise blank. The sheet's fire-wall sign at the south end is not built: the kit has one party wall, and the range stands against an open gable, as 1720's does. Every opening's s counts from the party wall's inner face on the alley wall, from the south end on the yard wall, from the gable on the range's alley wall, from the range's far end on its yard wall, and from the piece's south end on its front wall, as the kit lays them. The stable's mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, centred where it stands (s 5.135); the range's as a sash centred where it stands (s 4.44). The carriage bay (3.0 m clear) with the loft hatch over it toward the north end, and a man door with a loft sash over it toward the south end, are the kit's; the yard wall, south of the one-storey piece, has a door onto the workyard between two stable sash with loft sash over them; the range has a door in its yard wall at its middle, so that it opens on the yard. The one-storey piece is built on the kit's lean-to fitting, standing on the lot line against the party wall (its north wall stops at the party wall's return), under a single-pitch roof at the kit's 20 degrees, 3.9 m high where it dies into the yard wall and 2.49 m at its front, with the kit's stable (Dutch) door in its front wall; the sheet draws no roof and no opening on it. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at 30 degrees over the 7.83 m span, as the deep stables took; the range under the kit's flat roof, flush with the alley and yard faces. No external stair, ramp, wing or ventilator: the sheet draws none. Not built: the sheet's two solid dots, inside the stable's south-east corner and the range's (the sign 1726's record reads as a vertical steam boiler; no stack is drawn). The workyard is paved from the yard door to the 1730 house's rear wall line (column 2676.97), 15.11 m east of the yard wall, the walk 1.55 m south of the stable's middle, where the door is, clear of the house's frame back porch.

The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, walls '12 8' and, on the alley wall about 3.3 m from the north wall, the key's window symbol with a dot for each storey (openings in the first and second storeys there); it shows no other opening, no roof and no yard surface. The alley wall carries a stable sash and a loft sash over it where the sheet's mark stands, a man door with a loft sash over it at the north end, and the kit's carriage bay (3.0 m clear) with the loft hatch and hoist over it toward 18th Street. The yard wall a door onto the workyard between two stable sash and two loft sash. The south end, on the 18th Street line, is the kit's open gable with two stable sash, the loft door over the middle and an attic sash in the peak; the north end is the kit's party wall, because 1730's alley building stands against its western half (the sheet draws the two on one line from the alley to about 7.6 m back). A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at 30 degrees, as 1812's (T-2321): 40 degrees would stand the ridge 6.4 m over the eaves of a 15.3 m deep building. No external stair, ramp, lean-to or wing: the sheet draws none. No ventilator (restriction ventilator_needs_evidence). The workyard is paved from the yard door to the house's rear wall line.

#
# Pinned to an exact binary rather than a version range because bpy is a stateful
# tool whose defaults and operators shift between releases; version pinning is what
# buys back determinism. The bpy pip wheel is a documented fallback, but the binary
# is preferred: the wheel hard-couples Blender's minor version to a specific CPython,
# which makes agent sandboxes fragile.
#
# Verified working 2026-08-09: headless geometry, custom float attributes, smart UV
# project, Cycles CPU AO bake, GLB export — all green in ~0.8 s for a test mesh.

coach_house.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick and the one window mark is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1834-stable-1935. The sheet gives the outline of the stable and of the one-storey piece against its yard wall at the north end, '2' and '1' storeys, the brick, and one of the key's window marks on the alley wall, a cross with a dot for each storey (the sign 1816's and 1824's alley walls carry), 7.87 m from the north wall (row 3308.72). It draws no fire-wall sign at either end. The kit stands its one party wall at the north end, on the lot line, where the sheet draws one wall against 1828's building, and its open gable at the south end, over the open strip. The mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, centred where it stands (s counts from the party wall's inner face, 0.33 m in, on the alley wall, and from the gable end on the yard wall). The rest of the alley wall is the kit's laid out for 16.3 m: two carriage bays 3.0 m clear, the loft hatch and hoist over the northern one and a loft sash over the other, a man door between the northern bay and the mark, and a stable sash and loft sash toward the south end. The yard wall, south of the one-storey piece, has two stable sash with loft sash over them and a door onto the workyard where the walk to the house meets it. The one-storey piece is built on the kit's lean-to fitting, standing on the lot line against the party wall as 1730's does (T-1932): 7.89 m along the yard wall, 3.09 m deep, its single-pitch roof rising to 3.9 m where it dies into the yard wall; a stable (Dutch) door and a sash in its front, both the kit's. The sheet breaks the wall line between the piece and the stable over about 1.5 m (2.85 to 4.32 m from the north wall), an opening between the two inside; it is not built, since the piece covers it. The kit's 40-degree gable runs its ridge along the alley, 3.15 m from eave to ridge over the 7.52 m span, with no dormer. The workyard is paved from the yard door 13.66 m east to the west face of the house's rear porch (sheet column 988.37, rows 3276.22-3357.89, drawn yellow and lettered OPEN 1st IR.CL.2nd), the walk 0.8 m south of the building's middle, inside the porch's width. Not built: the solid dot inside the piece (the key's vertical steam boiler; the kit has no stack and the sheet draws none) and a small cross inside the stable's south-west corner, which 1630's shed record reads as the key's shingle-roof sign: if it is, the kit's slate is wrong here, and the liberty says so.

The sheet gives the outline, '1½' storeys, the brick, walls '12', the key's fire-wall sign at the east end of the north wall on the lot line, an open circle printed inside the south-west corner (a key sign this record does not read, and does not build), and no window mark. The party wall stands at the north end on the 1701/1709 lot line, where the sheet puts the fire wall, and the open gable faces south over the rest of the lot. The carriage bay (3.0 m clear), a man door and a stable sash are on the west wall's ground storey, nothing above them: the half-storey's walls (loft_m 1.2 m) leave no room under the eave, so the loft hatch is in the south gable, over a stable door, between two stable sash. Two stable sash light the back wall. A gable roof with its ridge along the west wall at 30 degrees over the 15.57 m span, as the deep stables on the alley across the avenue (1736, 1726) took. No stair, ramp, lean-to, wing, workyard or ventilator: the sheet draws none, and no drive to the building is drawn or built.

variant.note: A full-height projection: a shallow three-storey pavilion 4 m wide and 0.6 m out, two windows a floor, finished with a deep cornice and a flat tin deck where a house's main roof would take it over.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the 1874 engraving's long principal-storey window: its round head stands 6.3 m over grade on T-2437's camera, 4.3 m over the 2.0 m floor, and the porch's balustrade hides its foot, so it runs down to a 0.75 m sill as the main wall's do

variant.note: A one-storey canted bay window under a flared, bracketed hood (T-2408), sized to 1620 Prairie's 1874 engraving through its solved camera: 1.94 m of front 0.58 m out on 45-degree cheeks, two round-headed lights in the front and blank cheeks (0.82 m of cheek on a 0.58 m projection leaves no room for a recessed light), a deep eaves on a console at each corner of the front over a row of modillions, and a slated hood that leaves the eaves nearly flat and steepens to the wall, as the engraving draws it. The flare's numbers and the brackets' sizes are the kit's, RECONSTRUCTED.

windows.why_not_ordinary: a grouped window: two narrow round-headed lights either side of a mullion, the pair 1620 Prairie's 1874 engraving draws in its bay's front, sized to the engraving's heights on T-2437's camera (lights 3.09-5.71 m over grade)

coach_house.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick and the sheet's two window marks is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1620-stable-1932. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, walls '12 8' on its north and south walls, and two of the key's window marks: on the alley wall about 9.19 m from the north wall line with a dot for each storey (openings in both storeys there), and on the south wall about 3.55 m from the alley line with one dot (an opening in the first storey only). It shows no other opening, no roof and no yard surface. The alley wall carries a stable sash and a loft sash over it where its mark stands, a man door with a loft sash over it at the north end, the kit's carriage bay (3.0 m clear) with the loft hatch over it, and two more stable sash toward the south end with a loft sash over the last; the south end is the kit's open gable with one stable sash where the sheet's one-dot mark stands, and nothing over it, as the mark says; the yard wall a door onto the workyard at its middle between two stable sash and two loft sash. The north end is the kit's party wall, because the sheet draws 1616's crossed building against it along its whole width. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at the kit's 40 degrees over a 7.36 m span: about 3.1 m from eave to ridge. No external stair, ramp, lean-to or wing: the sheet draws none (Robinson 1886's ell at the north end is not on it). No ventilator (restriction ventilator_needs_evidence). The workyard is paved from the yard door toward the house's rear wall (25.5 m east of the yard wall).

coach_house.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick and the one window mark is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1824-stable-1935. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick and one of the key's window marks on the alley wall, the same sign 1816's alley wall carries twice (a cross with a dot for each storey): 8.34 m from the north wall (row 2648.9). The mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it (s counts from the north party wall's inner face, 0.33 m in). The rest of the alley wall is the kit's laid out for a building this long (17.6 m, as 1816's 22.4 m is laid out): two carriage bays 3.0 m clear, the loft hatch and hoist over the northern one and a loft sash over the other, a man door between the northern bay and the mark, and a stable sash and loft sash toward the south end. The yard wall has a door onto the workyard where the walk to the house meets it, and three stable sash with loft sash over them. Both ends are party walls (the sheet's fire-wall signs), so there is no open gable. The kit's 40-degree gable runs its ridge along the alley. The workyard is paved from the yard door 9.08 m east to the west wall of the house's brick body (sheet column 964.6, rows 2585.7-2799.5), the walk on that wall's middle, 1.75 m south of the building's. A small ring the sheet draws inside the building's south-west corner (about column 590, row 2817) is not read and builds nothing.

The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, walls '12 12', a stable's X, the key's fire-wall sign at the alley end of its north wall and of its south wall, a dashed partition 1.32 m inside the east wall, and two of the key's window marks: on the alley wall about 5.67 m from the north wall line and 5.37 m from the south with a dot for each storey (openings in both storeys there), and on the north wall about 7.69 m from the alley line with one dot (an opening in one storey, built in the first as 1612's and 1620's one-dot marks are). The kit is built in MIRROR IMAGE (`mirror`): its party wall stands at the south end, which carries no window, and rises the kit's 0.45 m above the roof (the sheet's fire-wall sign; 1700-1706's stable stands 1.9 m south of it, past the lot line); its open gable at the north end, on the 1636/1638 lot line over 1636's open rear yard, carries the sheet's one-dot mark. The sheet's fire-wall sign at the north end is not built: the kit has one party wall and one open gable, and the north end is the one with a window in it. Every opening's s counts from the party wall's inner face (the alley and yard walls' s from the south end and the north end respectively, as the kit lays them in mirror image; the gable's from the alley face). The alley mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, centred where it stands (s 5.04); the carriage bay (3.0 m clear) with the loft hatch over it toward the south end, and a man door with a loft sash over it toward the north end, are the kit's. The yard wall has a door onto the workyard at its middle between two stable sash and two loft sash; the north gable one stable sash where the sheet's mark stands and nothing over it. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at 30 degrees over the 10.46 m span, as the deep stables (1612, 1616, 1626, 1628, 1700, 1720, 1726, 1736) took, about 3.0 m from eave to ridge. No external stair, ramp, lean-to, wing or ventilator: the sheet draws none. Not built: the dashed partition (inside) and the sheet's solid dot inside the building about 1.3 m from its south wall and 4.7 m from the alley, the key's sign for a vertical steam boiler (the kit has no stack, and the sheet draws none). The workyard is paved from the yard door to the 1638 house's rearmost wall line on the trace, 9.42 m east of the yard wall.

variant.note: A full-height projection: a shallow three-storey pavilion 4 m wide and 0.6 m out, two windows a floor, finished with a deep cornice and a flat tin deck where a house's main roof would take it over.

each cheek's round-arched light between its two columns, read off the Grosvenor photograph in the west cheek (glass dark at x 374-392 px between the cheek's column at 350-360 and the angle's at 397-407; its crown at about y 520 under the capitals' band): 0.38 m clear, from the sill band at 3.15 m to 5.8 m under a 0.05 m band, 0.79 m along the 1.16 m cheek of T-2909's deeper plan, where its glass lands on the photograph's; the east cheek's by symmetry (T-2886, T-2909)

The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, walls '12', an open circle printed inside the south-west corner and a small mark at the south-east corner (key signs this record does not read, and does not build), and no window mark. The plan is the kit's rectangle sheared onto the sheet's parallelogram (skew_per_m 0.302: each metre south along the west wall steps it 0.302 m east; widths and openings are laid out along the lot line, so on the slanting walls each is about 4% longer than its s range). Turned to the lot: there is no alley here, so the kit's alley wall, with the carriage bay, is the WEST wall, facing the house's yard, and the kit's yard wall is the back wall to the tracks. The kit's party wall stands at the north end on the 1635/1637 lot line (the sheet draws no fire-wall sign there; the kit's own end), and the open gable faces south across the 1637/1701 lot line toward 1701's building about a metre away. On the west wall the carriage bay (3.0 m clear) under a loft hatch at its north end, then three stable sash and a man door along the 17 m wall, each under a loft sash; on the south gable a stable door between two sash, two loft sash over them; on the back wall two sash, each under a loft sash. The kit's 40-degree gable roof with its ridge along the slant. No stair, ramp, lean-to, wing, workyard or ventilator: the sheet draws none, and no drive to the building is drawn or built.

The sheet gives the outline of a stable 16.61 m along the alley by 10.11 m deep and of a one-storey range 6.93 m on south of it along the alley, 4.22 m deep, to the 1720/1726 lot line; '2' storeys and '1'; the brick; a stable's X over the stable alone; and two of the key's window marks: one on the stable's alley wall 8.90 m from its north wall line and 7.72 m from its south, a dot for each storey (openings in both storeys there), and one on the range's alley wall 6.79 m from the stable's south wall line, with one dot. It draws no fire-wall sign. The kit stands as drawn: its party wall at the north end, 1.20 m short of the 1712/1720 lot line, where nothing stands against it (the kit's end wall; the sheet's north wall has no window mark); its open gable at the south end, which the range covers to 3.45 m and which is otherwise blank. Every opening's s counts from the party wall's inner face on the alley wall, from the south end on the yard wall, from the gable on the range's alley wall and from the range's far end on its yard wall, as the kit lays them. The stable's mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, centred where it stands (s 8.57). The carriage bay (3.0 m clear) with the loft hatch over it toward the north end, and a man door with a loft sash over it toward the south end, are the kit's; the yard wall has a door onto the workyard at its middle between four stable sash, with loft sash over the outer two; the range has a door in its yard wall at its middle, so that it opens on the yard. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at 30 degrees over the 10.11 m span, as the deep stables (1616, 1612, 1626, 1628, 1700, 1736) took; the range under the kit's flat roof. windows.why_not_ordinary: the basement light under the arched window, read off the photograph: about 1.9 m wide and 1 m high from about 0.1 m over the walk, barred with ironwork; built 0.86 m clear on a 0.22 m sill over a 0.1 m plinth, its sill stone just clear of the plinth's top and its head at the print's 1.08 m (T-2953; the light's scrolls are T-2544's)
the first storey's large round-arched window, read off the photograph: 1.45 m between its jambs, its sill 0.58 m over the floor and its crown about 2.5 m over the sill (T-2543)

the second storey's paired window under its transom lights, read off the photograph: 2.3 m across the pair (T-2543); T-3091: its sashes' heads at about 8.04 m under a heavy stone bar to 8.23 m, a low light glazed in small squares over each to 8.64 m (tiers), on a 0.24 m mullion

grade_m.note: the app's ground over the house's lowest foot, measured in the published 1904 app (T-3206): the yard is lifted onto it so the lawn and the walk are not under it

coach_house.note: Everything but the plan is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1812-coach-house-2321. The sheet gives the outline, the two storeys and the brick; it shows no opening, roof or yard surface. The alley wall carries the kit's carriage bay (3.0 m clear) with the loft hatch and hoist over it, a man door, a stable sash and two loft sash; the yard wall a door onto the workyard between two stable sash and two loft sash over them. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley, as the kit builds it, at 30 degrees rather than the kit's 40, because the building is 14.6 m deep and 40 degrees would stand the ridge 6.1 m over the eaves, as tall again as the walls. No external stair, ramp, lean-to or wing: the sheet draws none, and both ends stand against neighbours. No ventilator (restriction ventilator_needs_evidence). The workyard is paved from the yard door to the house's rear wall line, which the sheet draws 6.22 m east of the coach house (column 992.5).
